source.title: Improving Generalization of Pre-trained Language Models via Stochastic Weight Averaging
source.authors: Peng Lu; I. Kobyzev; Mehdi Rezagholizadeh; Ahmad Rashid; A. Ghodsi; P. Langlais

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper through its appendix; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares test-set performance and Hessian-based flatness after standard fine-tuning versus stochastic weight averaging on pretrained language models. This is a different method and setting from the mapped versions, but its results bear on generalization performance and a measured property associated with the gap.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own comparisons of SWA with regular fine-tuning and its Hessian measurements. Results about KD and SAM are comparison methods. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, architecture comparisons, adaptive-versus-SGD generalization, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study tests adapted SWA for pretrained language-model fine-tuning, which none of V1–V8 names. Its Hessian eigenvalue and trace measurements do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure, generalization-gap correlation, or ranking against alternative measures. Using AdamW and tuning batch size do not provide the comparisons required by V4 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase accurately captures the reported performance improvements and MRPC curvature result. The authors conclude that their adapted SWA matches state-of-the-art KD performance on GLUE and improves regular fine-tuning on question answering and summarization. They claim no additional computation cost, although Table 4 reports 1.08× fine-tuning time; 'little added computation' is a more faithful description of that measurement.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes pretrained language models with SWA, averaging checkpoints along the optimization trajectory; it does not test the mapped claim's natural-label versus random-label generalization setup or the specific interventions in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports better performance with a high constant learning rate than a cyclical learning rate on SST-2 and MRPC; it also describes task-dependent averaging choices, including averaging over steps and starting SWA after 50% of training for most NLU tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Adapted SWA improves the reported GLUE average from 81.3 to 82.2 and improves all reported SQuAD and XSum metrics over regular fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adapted stochastic weight averaging can improve pretrained language-model performance on the tested downstream NLP tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: For DistilRoBERTa on MRPC, SWA reduces the reported largest Hessian eigenvalue from 60.22 to 1.19 and trace from 76.4 to 4.72, excluding embedding layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SWA yields lower measured Hessian curvature than regular fine-tuning in this model-task comparison.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2022
record.problems: No uncertainty values are stated for the main benchmark tables. The flatness analysis is shown for one model and dataset, excludes embedding layers, and does not measure train-test gap directly. The paper says larger model sizes were not explored due to limited computation resources.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted; 16 rows are extracted from Tables 1–3 and Appendix A, Table 5. Figure 1's constant-versus-cyclical learning-rate values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text, so no numeric rows were created for that figure.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label training or natural-versus-random-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep through and beyond zero training error.
No adaptive-optimizer-versus-SGD comparison or switching intervention.
No held-out performance comparison across batch sizes under controlled epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measurement, generalization-gap ranking, similarly low training-loss comparison, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No results test a listed version, so no verdict labels apply. R13 and R15 are comparator values already included as baselines in R14 and R16 and should not be counted as independent comparisons. The record's assertion that no results were omitted overlooks per-task GLUE results and Table 4, but these omissions do not bear on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test performance.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond an interpolation threshold.
AdamW is used as the optimizer, but there is no comparison with SGD or momentum SGD on generalization.
The study measures Hessian eigenvalue and trace, not magnitude-aware sharpness, and does not compare gap rankings across networks of one convolutional family.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining comparison.

relation.reason: The paper discusses flatness and generalization as motivation, but neither tests nor operationally uses the specific finding in any listed version. AdamW use and batch-size tuning do not test V4 or V5.

tranche.reason: SWA fine-tuning performance and raw Hessian curvature measure constructs outside V1–V8. The study does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap correlation, or ranking against alternative measures.

source_check.notes: R1–R12 report the study's own method comparisons rather than evidence for a listed version; R13 and R15 duplicate comparator values in R14 and R16. The authors claim no added computation, but Table 4 reports SWA time of 1.08× regular fine-tuning.
